blocks.prompt: 3. Find the equation of lines represented by \(5x^{2} + 6xy + y^{2} = 0\) and also find measure of the angle between them. (Problems 1-5)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh homogeneous second degree equation hai (har term ki degree 2), is liye Theorem 8 ke mutabiq yeh origin se guzarne wali do lines ka jora hai.
Diya kya hai? Sirf joint equation. Find kya karna hai? Dono lines alag alag, aur un ke darmiyan angle.
Rule kaunsa? Lines ke liye middle term split kar ke factorization, kyunke joint equation asal mein do lines ka product hai.
Angle ke liye formula \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}}{a + b}\), jo seedha coefficients se angle deta hai.
Plan: split, factor, lines; phir \(a\), \(h\), \(b\), phir angle; aakhir mein slopes se tasdeeq.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(5x^{2} + 6xy + y^{2} = 0\).
Maloom karna: dono lines ki equations aur un ke darmiyan angle \(\theta\).
Tareeqa: pehle middle term split kar ke factorize karenge; zero-product rule se dono lines milengi. Phir equation ko \(ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0\) se mila kar \(a\), \(h\), \(b\) parhenge aur Section 5.9 ka formula (iv) lagayenge.

Middle term split karein
\[5x^{2} + 5xy + xy + y^{2} = 0\]
Kyun: aise do numbers chahiye jin ka product \(5 \times 1 = 5\) ho (pehla coefficient guna aakhri coefficient) aur jama \(6\) ho (beech wala coefficient). Woh numbers \(5\) aur \(1\) hain: product 5, jama 6. Dono positive, kyunke product aur jama dono positive hain.

Jore bana kar factorize karein
\[5x(x + y) + y(x + y) = 0\]
\[(5x + y)(x + y) = 0\]
Kyun: pehle do terms mein se common nikala, phir aakhri do mein se. Dono jagah ek hi bracket bacha, yahi nishani hai ke split sahi tha; phir woh bracket bahar nikal liya.
Dhyan dein: doosre jore se common nikalte waqt sign ka khayal rakhiye, warna bracket match nahi karega.

Lines alag karein
\[5x + y = 0 \quad \text{aur} \quad x + y = 0\]
Kyun: product zero tabhi hota hai jab koi ek factor zero ho. Har factor ek line hai, aur dono mein constant term nahi, is liye dono origin se guzarti hain.

\(a\), \(h\), \(b\) parhein
\[a = 5,\quad h = 3,\quad b = 1\]
\[h^{2} - ab = 9 - 5 = 4\]
\[\sqrt{h^{2} - ab} = 2\]
Kyun: \(a\) \(x^{2}\) ka coefficient, \(b\) \(y^{2}\) ka, aur \(h\) \(xy\) ke coefficient ka AADHA. \(h^{2} - ab\) positive aaya, to Theorem 8 ke mutabiq lines real aur alag hain; yeh hamari factorization se bhi milta hai.
Dhyan dein: negative \(b\) ho to \(-ab\) positive ban jata hai; signs dhyan se lagaiye.

Lines ke darmiyan angle
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{2(2)}{5 + 1} = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}\]
\[\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = 33.69^{\circ}\]
Kyun: formula (iv) mein values rakhi. \(\tan\theta\) positive aaya to angle seedha acute (90 se chhota) hai. Calculator degree mode mein hona chahiye. Yeh wahi equation hai jo Section 5.9 ki Example 17 mein thi; answer key mein bhi \(33.69^{\circ}\) hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[m_{1} = -5,\quad m_{2} = -1\]
\[\dfrac{-5 - (-1)}{1 + 5} = -\dfrac{2}{3},\quad \left|-\dfrac{2}{3}\right| = \dfrac{2}{3} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: dono lines ke slopes nikal kar purane formula \(\tan\theta = \left|\dfrac{m_{1} - m_{2}}{1 + m_{1}m_{2}}\right|\) se bhi wahi value aayi; is ka matlab hamara jawab pakka hai.
